title: 2017 AMC 10B Problem 6
statement: What is the largest number of solid \(2\)-in \(\times\) \(2\)-in \(\times\) \(1\)-in blocks that can fit in a \(3\)-in \(\times\) \(2\)-in \(\times\) \(3\)-in box?

solutions.text:
The volume of the large solid object is \(3\cdot 3\cdot 2 = 18\) and volume of the smaller object is \(2\cdot 2\cdot 1=4.\) This means we can fit at most \(4\) of the small objects.

We can make this happen by putting \(3\) of the small objects in a \(3 \times 2 \times 2\) rectangular prism, and then we have a \(3 \times 2 \times 1\) space left where we can place one small object.

Thus, the correct answer is B .
hints: Start with the volume upper bound
Then check that four blocks really can be arranged
